chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Imam as-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
He said: Three people do not receive the greeting of peace: the one walking with a funeral procession, the one walking to the congregational Friday prayer, and the one in the bathhouse.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people that should not be greeted with salam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates three specific social and ritual contexts where the greeting of peace is withheld, highlighting the importance of situational awareness in Shia etiquette. The exclusion of those in the bathhouse (*hammam*) reflects the state of minor ritual impurity or modesty, while the omission for those proceeding to Friday prayer emphasizes the solemnity of the congregational journey. This ruling underscores the nuanced interplay between social interaction and ritual purity in daily Muslim life.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-31 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Imam as-Sadiq (MGB) saying,
“Do not greet those who are attending a funeral procession, those who are going to the congregational prayers, and those who are in the bath.”
